ENG 101.name: English and Composition I
ENG 101.description: The central basis of ENG 101 is to introduce students to an academic approach to thinking, reading, speaking and writing in an integrated, meaningful manner such that they are able to apply the skills learnt to their departmental studies. In addition, the ENG 101 course aims to further develop the students' linguistic accuracy and range in English.

ENG 102.name: English and Composition II
ENG 102.description: The central basis of ENG 102 is to consolidate students' academic approach to thinking, reading, speaking and writing and language usage, as initiated in ENG 101. In addition, the ENG 102 course aims to develop the students' abilities to synthesize and evaluate information and conduct basic, independent research.

ENG 117.name: Advanced English Grammar I
ENG 117.description: This course is designed specifically to help students to further develop competency in grammar, vocabulary and modes of written expression under timed conditions. In order to improve their self-editing skills, students will keep a portfolio of their written work.

ENG 118.name: Advanced English Grammar II
ENG 118.description: This course is designed to build on the skills developed in ENG 117, specifically by helping literature students to improve their competency in grammar, vocabulary and modes of written expression under timed conditions. In order to improve their self-editing skills, students will keep a portfolio of their written work.

ENG 206.name: Business Communication
ENG 206.description: Theoretical insights into business practices, practical applications in business networking, professional communication in business environments, business correspondence, persuasive speaking, presentation skills, interpersonal communication, professional development.

ENG 312.name: Introduction to Creative Writing
ENG 312.description: Creative writing, fiction, writerly craft, short story, written sketches, creative process, inspiration techniques, expression in English, professional examples, critical audience, personal development, storytelling, literary elements, narrative structure, constructive critique.

ENG 401.name: Technical Report Writing and Presentation
ENG 401.description: The object of this course is to assist engineering students in effectively presenting various types of information in both the written and oral modes. Students will be expected to become competent in writing and organizing technical reports and in effectively presenting academic and technical papers. The tasks performed as part of the course will mirror the tasks students will be expected to do in their prospective professional lives and in their faculty classes.

ENG 406.name: Graduate Writing and Presentation Seminar
ENG 406.description: ENG 406 is primarily a writing seminar for graduate students. The course will focus on issues of style, voice, logic, grammars, and audience awareness in students' written work. In addition, students will learn and discuss how to present their papers effectively to an audience of peers. The objective of the course is to develop in students a scholarly identity within the conventions of their discipline. Students' own writing will serve as the basis for class discussions.
